sections.overview: Scolytus mali is a bark beetle in the weevil family Curculionidae, subfamily Scolytinae.
sections.identification: Adults are small, cylindrical beetles; the species account gives a length of about three to four and a half millimetres.
sections.habitat: It colonises physiologically weakened trunks and branches, including fruit trees.
sections.diet: Larvae develop beneath bark in the tissues of host trees, including apple, pear and plum in the Slovenian records.
sections.behavior: The female makes a longitudinal maternal gallery, from which larval galleries branch transversely.
sections.reproduction: In Slovenia, two generations are reported in a year, with adult emergence in late spring and again in late summer.
sections.ecology: Although fruit trees are its principal recorded hosts, the specialist account also lists some wild Rosaceae, elms and hazels.
sections.conservation: These sources give no global conservation assessment.
